To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bauxite residues are available worldwide at a multi‐millions tonne scale, and can contain considerable amounts (e.g. up to 1% by weight) of CRMs, which can be recovered from bauxite residues using a variety of technologies, and that the recovery of these materials is beneficial for both the environment and the economy.
bauxite residue can be a secondary source of critical raw materials, which is beneficial for the environment, health and society.

bauxite residues constitute a multi‐million‐tonnes source of CRMs and that re‐use / re‐processing of these residues can generate significant environmental and health benefits, in particular if compared with the alternative of conventional primary mining.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials and processes that will enable the efficient recovery of critical elements from waste streams, in particular from bauxite residue.
the recovery of valuable materials from bauxite residues.
the development of new and more efficient methods for the production of alumina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bauxite residues are not a waste but a resource, and that the recovery of CRMs from bauxite residues should be considered a viable option.
the benefits of bauxite re‐use are manifold and that the economic value of CRM recovery is only one factor in a complex equation.
the benefits from re‐using bauxide residues for CRM recovery outweigh the associated challenges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bauxite residue is a valuable secondary resource, which can be re‐used in several ways.
the bauxite residue can be considered a secondary resource for critical raw materials.
the recovery of CRMs from bauxite residues has the potential to contribute to a more sustainable alumina industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bauxite residue is not just waste, but a valuable resource.
the benefits of bauxite-residue re-use/recycling extend far beyond the economic value of CRM recovery, and that the latter can be quantified.

bauxite residue is a resource that is not only rich in critical raw materials (e.g. rare earth elements) but that also has a high potential of providing other benefits beyond (critical) raw material recovery.
